specialistReviews.finding: Snapshot includes p_user_id subject IDs not always actors and cannot confuse customer recipient vs admin caller.
specialistReviews.resolution: Store exact named args with independent binding classification and annotate recipient flows.

challenge.scenario: Developer adds a privileged admin_queue_office_email_v7 RPC in a new API route.
challenge.finding: A new service-role caller may bypass authenticated actor and tenant scope.
challenge.resolution: AST scanner detects new RPC and fails --check until it is classified/reviewed.

challenge.scenario: An existing owner transfer p_actor changes from userId to form.get(userId).
challenge.finding: Actor spoof might reappear despite earlier F26 tests.
challenge.resolution: Exact normalized p_actor expression snapshot drift causes hard fail.

challenge.scenario: A high-level helper passes input.instanceId from request JSON into Office mutation.
challenge.finding: Tenant context can be confused across shops.
challenge.resolution: Changed named instance arg is detected and requires upstream provenance review, never assumed safe.

challenge.scenario: Communication enqueue p_user_id is a customer recipient ID.
challenge.finding: Mislabeling it as a privileged operator leads to misleading audit findings.
challenge.resolution: Classify separately as recipient, not verified actor.

challenge.scenario: Two calls of same RPC are present in a file.
challenge.finding: Snapshot keyed only by function name would silently cover one of them.
challenge.resolution: Assign deterministic ordinal by encounter order and store each distinct call.

challenge.scenario: A newly added TypeScript TSX page calls Office list RPC.
challenge.finding: A page bypass can leak private metadata.
challenge.resolution: Scan both .ts and .tsx under src and reject untracked call.

challenge.scenario: Dynamic function name is used as a call target.
challenge.finding: Scanner cannot identify exact permissions needed, false certainty.
challenge.resolution: Count and report dynamic rpc calls as blind spots, reject new dynamic Office-like call changes on sensitive paths.

challenge.scenario: Snapshot is regenerated by generator without security review.
challenge.finding: Source-only inventory marked safe despite malicious RPC.
challenge.resolution: --print never writes; --check reads frozen reviewed file only, describe manual review requirement.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: F26 audited 3 Team Chat entry points and 191/191 source/API tests but broader Office/Communication Hub has about 55 RPC calls across 35 files with intermediate input.userId, actorId, service-only actor-scoped SQL, and p_user_id customer recipients. Future changes can silently route caller-controlled actor/tenant values to privileged service-role RPC without being noticed by tests. Introduce a TypeScript AST-based source-only inventory of all statically named Office/communication/chat/thread/support/email/inbound RPC calls including literal argument bindings, with manually reviewed baseline classification for actor vs customer subject and fail-closed drift gate/test. Do not rewrite product logic or claim JWT/RLS native security proof.
observableOutcomes: Inventory AST checks all TypeScript and TSX src files for literal .rpc calls matching Office/Communication Hub RPC names; prints accurate call/file counts and snapshot of p_actor, p_instance_id, p_user_id.

Reviewed canonical snapshot lists each existing sensitive RPC call with file, name and argument expression, classifies authenticated actor vs recipient/system-scoped with source-only attestation; caller-controlled deltas require explicit review.

--check exits nonzero if a new RPC name/callsite appears, an actor/instance argument expression changes, a call is deleted/renamed or a reviewed entry becomes undocumented; --print is nonmutating for review.
Unit tests assert baseline coverage, deliberate new RPC and forged actor mutation fail closed against inventory comparator, source-only classification, no network calls.
Non-authoritative dated audit note explicitly separates 55 source calls from native authenticated JWT/RLS and provider integration and flags service-only p_actor attack surface.
No business SQL/route/actor runtime or customer baseline changes, Control Plane and regression PASS.
unresolvedRisks: Static callsite/argument matching cannot prove transitive helper trust, signing of a Supabase JWT, or runtime RLS; manual review and dynamic tests needed.
Functions using nonliteral names or indirect RPC wrappers are not recognized; the script reports blind spots and limits claims.
A snapshot may be consciously changed to accept an unsafe actor mapping: review and stronger dynamic tests required before main acceptance.
Recipient p_user_id in enqueue_communication_v2 represents a customer subject, not an authenticated actor; review classification must not conflate these.
